text: There is currently no direct evidence in PubMed linking Nystatin, a polyene antifungal, to the modulation of MAP2K1 (MEK1) in the context of melanoma. While some polyenes have been investigated for off-target effects on mammalian cholesterol-rich lipid rafts—which can serve as signaling platforms for receptor tyrosine kinases—any potential interaction with MAP2K1 would likely be an indirect consequence of altered membrane dynamics rather than a direct pharmacological inhibition. Consequently, this interaction remains speculative and lacks validation in current oncological literature.
